decisions.reason: Attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1 (pinned by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl) whose install lifecycle script runs node-gyp configure build and fails node-gyp's find VS probe for missing MSVC — not pnpm or network unreliability.

Shows the top-level static flock import makes fs-ext load on Windows before branch selection, so --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install time to service boot; cites both the fixture and the card saying the module must exist and load.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 with CreateSemaphoreW/Wait/Release named kernel semaphore from POSIX flock(2), concludes fs-ext is dead code on Windows justifying a load-only stub, keeps POSIX on the real binding, and preserves the semaphore as the actual Windows lock.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: win32-guarded install script, entry with a pure-JS flock fallback that warns once and calls the callback with success (compatible callable/callback shape), registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml, and reinstall/module-load/service-boot plus POSIX regression checks.

Explicitly honors the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint (installing VS listed among rejected alternatives) and uses only the repository-managed patch, touching no upstream repository or published dependency.
Cites the full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 with its edge, migration recipe and verification plan, and connects it to the fs-ext install failure and the Windows patch plan — not the bare ID.

caps.reason: Installing Visual Studio is affirmatively rejected as forbidden by the owner; the plan requires no toolchain.
The plan skips the build only inside a patch that also makes the statically imported entry loadable; --ignore-scripts alone is explicitly rejected.
Uses the repository-managed pnpm patchedDependencies mechanism; forking/vendoring and upstream edits are rejected.
Windows locking stays on the named semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock; the stub is win32-gated, not a universal no-op.
